items.stem: Which TWO practices help confirm that an energy-saving measure actually delivered savings? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Establishing a measured baseline before the change
options.rationale: A baseline is essential to attribute savings.

options.text: Comparing adjusted post-measure consumption against that baseline
options.rationale: Measurement and verification compares against the adjusted baseline.

options.text: Assuming the vendor's brochure figure is the realised saving
options.rationale: Brochure figures are not verified savings.
Cosmetic work does not verify savings.

items.explanation: A baseline is essential to attribute savings.

items.stem: A BMS trend shows a zone's heating valve and cooling coil both active at the same time. What does this most likely indicate?

options.text: A control fault causing simultaneous heating and cooling that wastes energy
options.rationale: Simultaneous heating and cooling is a classic controls fault wasting energy.

options.text: Optimal comfort control working as designed
options.rationale: Fighting heating and cooling is wasteful, not optimal.

options.text: That the building envelope is perfectly sealed
options.rationale: Envelope sealing is unrelated to this control conflict.
The trend reflects control state, not a meter fault.

items.explanation: Simultaneous heating and cooling is a classic controls fault wasting energy.
